models._description: Adds ldaps One2many to res.company.ldap (copy=True, groups=base.group_system) — per-company ordered list of LDAP configs
Adds ldaps One2many related='company_id.ldaps' (readonly=False) so LDAP servers are edited from the General Settings page
Overrides _login / _check_credentials to fall back to LDAP bind, change_password to propagate to the directory, plus _set_empty_password (4 methods, no new stored fields)

behavioral_notes.observation: res.company.ldap is a pure-configuration model (_order='sequence', _rec_name='ldap_server') that stores one directory's connection wiring: ldap_server (default 127.0.0.1) + ldap_server_port (default 389), ldap_tls (request STARTTLS encryption on connect), ldap_binddn / ldap_password (the service account used to QUERY the directory — empty binddn means anonymous bind), ldap_base (DN of the user-search subtree scope) and ldap_filter (an arbitrary LDAP filter where each '%s' placeholder is substituted with the supplied login, e.g. '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user)(sAMAccountName=%s))' for Active Directory or '(|(mail=%s)(uid=%s))'; the filter MUST resolve to exactly one entry or the login is rejected). create_user (default True) decides whether a missing local account is auto-provisioned, and user is an optional Template User copied when provisioning. ldaps is a One2many on res.company so each company holds an ordered (sequence) list of directories tried in turn. The single ACL (ir.model.access) plus the group_system on the company.ldaps field means only system administrators may read/write these records — credentials are never exposed to ordinary users.

auth_ldap layers directory auth UNDER Odoo's native login: res.users._login first calls super()._login (local password check) and only on AccessDenied falls through to LDAP — and only if no local res_users row already exists for that login (an existing local user keeps its local credential, re-raising AccessDenied). It then iterates res.company.ldap._get_ldap_dicts() (sudo search_read of every configured server ordered by sequence) and calls _authenticate(conf, login, password) on each. _authenticate explicitly rejects an empty password up front (RFC 4513 — prevents an 'unauthenticated authentication' anonymous bind succeeding with a valid DN + blank password), resolves the user's DN via _get_entry, then opens a SECOND connection and does conn.simple_bind_s(dn, password): a successful bind IS the proof of identity (the directory, not Odoo, verifies the password). The first matching server wins, returning auth_method='ldap', mfa='default'. _check_credentials provides the same LDAP fallback for an already-known uid (re-auth / RPC), gated by env['interactive'] or not _rpc_api_keys_only() and only for credential type 'password'.

After a successful bind, _get_or_create_user(conf, login, ldap_entry) maps the external identity to a local res.users: it lower()/strip()s the login, runs a raw SQL 'SELECT id, active FROM res_users WHERE lower(login)=%s' and, if an ACTIVE row exists, returns it (idempotent login). If no row exists AND conf['create_user'] is set, it provisions a new user via _map_ldap_attributes — name comes from the LDAP 'cn' attribute (ldap_entry[1]['cn'][0]), login is the supplied login, company_id is the config's company, and email is filled only when the login itself is a valid email (tools.single_email_re). Creation runs as sudo() with no_reset_password context; if a Template User is configured it copy()s that user (inheriting groups/preferences), otherwise it plain create()s. If the user is absent and create_user is False it raises AccessDenied('No local user found ... and not configured to create one'). This is JIT account creation: the directory is the system of record for who may log in, Odoo mirrors only a thin local shadow account.

behavioral_notes.element: res.users.change_password -> res.company.ldap._change_password + _set_empty_password (password propagation to the directory & local-credential neutralisation)
behavioral_notes.observation: change_password is overridden so an LDAP user changing their password writes through to the directory: for each configured server it calls _change_password(conf, login, old, new) which resolves the DN, binds with the OLD password and issues ldap.passwd_s(dn, old, new) (the python-ldap extended PASSWD operation). On the first directory that accepts the change it calls _set_empty_password() — a raw 'UPDATE res_users SET password=NULL WHERE id=%s' that NULLs the local password column (with flush/invalidate around it) so the only valid credential remains the directory's; it then returns True without falling through to super(). If no directory accepts it, it defers to the standard local change_password. Net effect: LDAP-managed accounts never keep a usable local password hash, forcing every authentication back through the bind path.

behavioral_notes.element: res.company.ldap._connect / _query / test_ldap_connection (connection handling, referral/TLS options, admin test)
behavioral_notes.observation: _connect builds 'ldap://server:port', honours the auth_ldap.disable_chase_ref ICP (default True -> set OPT_REFERRALS OFF to stop AD referral chasing that breaks anonymous follow-ups), and calls start_tls_s() when ldap_tls is set; it returns an LDAPWrapper thin proxy exposing simple_bind_s/search_st/passwd_s/unbind. _query binds with the SERVICE account (binddn/password, defaulting to empty=anonymous) and runs search_st over ldap_base with SCOPE_SUBTREE and a 60s timeout, swallowing INVALID_CREDENTIALS/LDAPError into logged errors (returns [] on failure rather than raising). test_ldap_connection is an admin-facing action that attempts a bind with the configured service credentials and returns a display_notification (success / server-down / invalid-credentials / timeout / generic error) so an administrator can validate server reachability and the bind DN before going live.

No client-side footprint at all: extract_frontend reports present=false — zero JS/OWL components, registry adds, services, patches or asset bundles. The entire UI is the server-rendered res.config.settings General Settings page plus the res.company.ldap list/form views (1 list + 1 form) where an administrator enters server/port/TLS, bind DN, base DN and filter and clicks the Test Connection button. There is no login-page widget — LDAP is invisible to the end user, who simply types their normal login/password into the standard web login form and is transparently authenticated against the directory.

behavioral_notes.element: external LDAP/Active Directory directory integration (gap #7: outbound directory binds)
behavioral_notes.observation: auth_ldap is an outbound-integration module whose integration is NOT over HTTP, so extract_frontend's HTTP-oriented scan reports http_call_sites=0 / sdk_imports=[] / endpoints=[]. The real external dependency is the python-ldap library ('import ldap', declared in the manifest external_dependencies.python=['python-ldap'], apt python3-ldap): every authentication makes server-to-server LDAP-protocol binds/searches (ldap.initialize -> start_tls_s -> simple_bind_s -> search_st -> passwd_s) against a corporate directory — OpenLDAP, Microsoft Active Directory / Entra-on-prem, FreeIPA, 389-DS, etc. The target servers are admin-configured per res.company.ldap record (ldap_server:ldap_server_port, optionally TLS), not hardcoded; uses_api_keys=true reflects the stored service-account bind credentials (ldap_binddn/ldap_password). This is the trust pivot: a successful simple_bind_s with the user's own credentials at the directory is what authenticates them — Odoo delegates password verification entirely to the directory.

policies: Single ACL + group_system on res.company.ldap / res.company.ldaps: only system administrators may read/write directory configs and their stored service credentials
Bind-is-truth policy: identity is proven by a successful simple_bind_s with the user's own password at the directory; empty passwords are rejected (RFC 4513, no unauthenticated authentication)
Local-first, LDAP-fallback policy: native local auth runs first; LDAP is only tried on AccessDenied, and an existing local-only user is NOT overridden by LDAP
Provisioning policy: a missing local user is auto-created only when create_user is set (optionally copying a Template User); otherwise AccessDenied
Filter-uniqueness policy: ldap_filter must resolve to exactly one directory entry or the login is rejected
Credential-neutralisation policy: on directory password change the local password is NULLed (_set_empty_password) so the directory remains the sole credential authority

Module developer (overrides _authenticate / _map_ldap_attributes / _get_or_create_user for custom attribute mapping or group sync)

classification.rationale: auth_ldap is IT identity-and-access infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). It owns no business object of its own: its single real model res.company.ldap is pure connection configuration (server/port/TLS, bind DN, base DN, user filter), and everything else is an extension of res.users (credential-pipeline hooks), res.company and res.config.settings. It exists solely to let users authenticate to Odoo against an EXTERNAL corporate directory (OpenLDAP / Active Directory / Entra on-prem / FreeIPA) by delegating password verification to a server-to-server LDAP simple-bind, sitting beneath the login that every other module relies on. It creates no document chain, holds no customer/order/product/ledger data, and produces no primary-activity output, so it is 'support' rather than chain/shop/network. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' is the precise fit: this is the 'identity & access management' / 'external system integration' capability — a concrete running access-control runtime (LDAP bind fallback, service-account directory query, external-to-local identity mapping, JIT provisioning, password write-through). 11.0 'Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance and Resiliency' was considered because directory auth touches account-security governance, but rejected: 11.0 is the governance layer (control frameworks, audits, policy management), whereas auth_ldap is the technical implementation IT builds and operates — APQC places that under 8.0 (Develop and manage IT security / identity & access management). The classification mirrors the sibling auth_oauth / auth_totp / web records (all 8.0 / support).

standard_capabilities: Transparent LDAP / Active Directory authentication delegated to the directory via python-ldap simple-bind (user keeps the standard Odoo login form)
Per-company, sequence-ordered list of directory servers (res.company.ldap) configured from General Settings: server/port, TLS (STARTTLS), bind DN + password, base DN, login filter
Service-account directory query with subtree-scoped search and a login-to-entry LDAP filter (each '%s' replaced by the login; must resolve to exactly one entry)
Just-in-time local user provisioning on first directory login (name from cn, email from login, optional Template User copy)
Local-first / LDAP-fallback ordering — native password auth runs first; LDAP only on AccessDenied; existing local-only users untouched
Password write-through to the directory (passwd_s) on change_password, NULLing the local password so the directory stays the sole credential
Admin Test Connection action and an AD-referral-chasing toggle (auth_ldap.disable_chase_ref ICP)
typical_fits: Letting employees log in to Odoo with their existing Active Directory / corporate LDAP credentials out of the box (set server/base/filter, create_user=True)
Centralising password policy and account lifecycle in the corporate directory while Odoo holds only thin shadow accounts
Multi-company deployments where each company points at its own directory (ordered res.company.ldap list)
Securing the connection with STARTTLS and a dedicated read-only service bind DN for directory queries
common_gaps: Simple-bind / STARTTLS only — no out-of-box ldaps:// (port 636 implicit SSL), Kerberos/GSSAPI/SASL or certificate-based bind without customisation
No automatic LDAP-group -> Odoo-group/role mapping and no de-provisioning (disabling/deleting a user in the directory does NOT deactivate the Odoo shadow account)
Attribute mapping is hardcoded (name<-cn, email<-login-if-email-shaped) — richer profile sync (givenName/sn/department/phone) needs an _map_ldap_attributes override
ldap_filter must resolve to exactly one entry; ambiguous/duplicate directory entries silently fail the login
Stored service-account password is plain config (group_system-gated) — no vault/secret-manager integration; anonymous bind requires the directory to permit it
No connection pooling/caching — each authentication opens fresh binds; no failover beyond trying the next configured server in sequence
